assignments.note: 2026-03 Judge scores look good Best-of-N fails
assignments.why: Measures how a judge with decent global correlation fails at within-prompt best-of-N selection (audit), and shows explicit pairwise judging recovers most of the gain (pairwise paradigm).

assignments.note: 2026-03 Knowledge divergence and the value of debate for scalable oversight
assignments.why: Studies when debate is effective for oversight, a threshold in knowledge divergence between debaters and judge.

assignments.note: 2026-03 Many SWE-bench-passing PRs would not be merged
assignments.why: Shows the SWE-bench test-based verifier overstates agent capability against maintainer review, a verifier failure in an agent benchmark.

assignments.note: 2026-03 Mind the Sim2Real Gap in User Simulation
assignments.why: Measures fidelity of 31 LLM user simulators against 451 real people with a User-Sim Index (user simulation) on the tau-bench agent protocol, showing simulators inflate agent success (agent benchmark).
Systematises attacks on judges and adversarial robustness (audit) and judges used as defences (judge designs).
Agentic judges that use tools and live environments to inspect trajectories, measured in a meta-evaluation benchmark of judges with failure-mode analysis.
RL-trained reward model/verifier, built as a multi-turn tool-using agentic verifier with forward and backward agents.
Fine-tunes a 210M encoder judge distilled from an LLM judge (small-encoder trained judge), a recipe for an open single-pass classifier built from an existing encoder.

Systematic measurement of style, position and verbosity bias across five judges (audit), testing nine debiasing strategies (judge methods), with position and formatting bias as main subjects (presentation sensitivity).
Measures verdict flips under repeated identical judging and cross-judge agreement (audit), with strong position bias (picks A 72%) as a headline finding.

assignments.note: 2026-05 An Empirical Study of Automating Agent Evaluation
assignments.why: EvalAgent, an agentic evaluator that writes evaluation code for a target agent, compared against Agent-as-a-Judge (judge design), and the AgentEvalBench harness of 20 agents.

assignments.note: 2026-05 Generating and Refining Dynamic Evaluation Rubrics
assignments.why: Generates instance-level rubrics to improve an LLM judge, and iteratively refines the rubric generator from meta-judge rewards (self-improving evaluator loop).
Audits and repairs LLM judge rubrics, using pairwise human preference data as the signal for what people want.
Controlled interventions measure LLM judge accuracy on deep-research agent traces (audit of judges judging agent trajectories).
RACER routes between reasoning and non-reasoning judges under budget so extra compute is spent only where needed, after measuring where reasoning judges help or hurt.
Judge-reliability benchmark across languages measuring biases such as length preference and missed hallucinated tool calls, extended with perturbed agent trajectories.
Meta-evaluation dataset of human labels on LLM judges' critiques, scoring process-level (step) errors in tau-bench and DA-Code agent trajectories.
Benchmark measuring judge instability on long-form outputs (audit), testing whether rubrics and references improve judging.
Shows LLM-judged scores stored in agent memory inflate and compound (judge failure inside an agent loop), and proposes LUCID to de-bias the judged signal.
Multi-agent debate where an LLM judge reads debate logs, and the question of when to overturn majority voting over agents' answers (vote aggregation).
An in-world evaluator agent judges interactive agents, generating situations tied to criteria rather than scoring a fixed trajectory (generated tests).
Large-scale measurement of 21 judges' agreement, consistency and bias, with position bias coexisting with high test-retest reliability as a main finding.
Multilingual judge that self-improves by sending cross-lingually inconsistent verdicts back for reflection, using a cross-language consistency check as the trigger.
Measures the decision fidelity of LLM user simulators against real purchase outcomes, critiquing the tau-bench simulator that always reaches its goal.
Hybrid UI/API user-simulation toolkit for testing customer-facing agents, with coverage and failure-finding metrics for the evaluation harness.
Multi-turn benchmark with a persona-driven user simulator decoupled from the target, and a separate LLM judge scoring turns and final-intent completion with cross-judge and human checks.
Taxonomy for localising agent failures to model or harness, applied with an agent-as-a-judge method.
Releases OS-Shepherd trained reward-model judges and a benchmark for computer-use trajectory judges, measuring leniency bias and disagreement with benchmarks' own verifiers.
Detects SWE-bench tasks whose gold PR does not match the issue, a task-suite validity problem in an agent benchmark.
Evolves judge rubrics from a single query using synthetic pairwise responses and necessity tests (self-refining evaluator) to improve LLM judging.
